facts.activity_file: benching, battering and shoring an excavation

consequence.label: first aid or minor property damage

control_failures.control_label: benching, battering or shoring of an excavation

facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: audit finding - spot check of key safeguard at DZ-9201

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control EXCAVATION_SUPPORT: the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control SLOPE_MONITORING_RESPONSE: the response to slope monitoring alarms had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

recommendations: Confirm at the next spot check that the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation on DZ-9201 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in designing and controlling excavations, specifically benching, battering and shoring an excavation. DZ-9201 (earthmoving fleet) is in service for loading and dozing. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent. The kinetic energy involved is held as rotating equipment, and the recorded presentation was entanglement, impact, crush.
response.summary: On 7 August 2004 a planned spot check of DZ-9201 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop found the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation not effective.
